Introduction to Creating Forest Plots for Bayesian Meta Analyses

Source: vignettes/bayesfoRest.Rmd
bayesfoRest.Rmd

bayesfoRest draws forest plots from a fitted Bayesian meta-analysis. You fit the model with whichever backend you prefer (brms, bayesmeta, MetaStan, rstanarm, rstan, cmdstanr, bayesma, RoBMA or R2jags), then pass it to bayes_forest() together with the study-level data.

Prepare the data and fit a model 

library(metafor)
library(brms)
library(bayesfoRest)

# Compute log odds ratios with {metafor}
binary_es <- escalc(
  measure = "OR",
  ai = Event_Intervention, bi = Outcome_Intervention_No,
  ci = Event_Control, di = Outcome_Control_No,
  n1i = N_Intervention, n2i = N_Control,
  data = binary_outcome) |>
  dplyr::mutate(sei = sqrt(vi))

# Fit a random-effect meta-analysis with brms
model_bin <- brm(
  yi | se(sei) ~ 1 + (1 | Author),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = binary_es,
  prior = prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept) +
          prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd),
  iter = 4000,
  cores = parallel::detectCores(),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  silent = 2)

Create the forest plot

Name the columns that hold the study label, year and arm-level data. For a binary outcome these are the group sizes and event counts:

bayes_forest(
  model = model_bin,
  data = binary_es,
  measure = "OR",
  studyvar = Author,
  yearvar = Year,
  n_ctrl = N_Control,
  n_int = N_Intervention,
  event_ctrl = Event_Control,
  event_int = Event_Intervention,
  title = "Treatment Effect on Binary Outcome",
  subtitle = "Bayesian Random-Effect Meta-Analysis (Odds Ratio)",
  xlim = c(0.1, 3.5)
)

For a continuous outcome, use mean_ctrl, mean_int, sd_ctrl and sd_int in place of the event columns. For time-to-event and rate outcomes, use time_ctrl and time_int.

Common options

  • model_type: "random_effect" or "common_effect". Detected from the model when not given.
  • plot_output = "boxplot": horizontal boxplots instead of densities.
  • subgroup = TRUE, subgroupvar = Subgroup: one panel per subgroup.
  • re_min_k: show a common-effect model when an analysis or subgroup has fewer than this many studies, because tau is poorly identified with so few.
  • add_rob = TRUE: add risk of bias columns. Choose the tool with rob_tool ("rob2", "robins_i", "robins_e", "quadas2", "clarity", "rob_nma", "probast" or "probast_ai") and add a key with add_rob_legend = TRUE.
  • exclude_high_rob = TRUE: drop studies with an overall high risk of bias.

See ?bayes_forest for the full list, and the README for examples of the other plots: rob_plot(), overall_plot(), funnel_plot(), diagnostics(), sensitivity_plot(), ecdf_model_plot() and ecdf_prior_plot().
